notices.title: Thailand cut visa-free stays on Sep 15, 2026
notices.body: Most visa-free stays dropped from 60 to 30 days, and 21 nationalities now need an e-visa. Visa-free entry is for tourism only, so remote work or business needs a proper visa such as the DTV. One 30-day extension may be granted at an immigration office at the officer's discretion.

notices.title: China's visa-free trial runs through Dec 31, 2026
notices.body: Many passports (including the UK and Canada since Feb 17, 2026) can visit China visa-free for up to 30 days under a trial policy that is currently set to end Dec 31, 2026. Check before booking travel for 2027.

notices.title: Kazakhstan's QazETA becomes mandatory Jul 1, 2027
notices.body: Visa-free visitors should get a free QazETA travel authorization at qazeta.kz at least 72 hours before arriving. It's phased in: Aktau airport and some land borders from Nov 1, 2026, Astana and Almaty airports from Jan 1, 2027, and all other entry points from Mar 1, 2027. Until Jul 1, 2027 you won't be turned away without one, but after that you can be. It's valid 180 days for multiple entries and doesn't extend your visa-free stay.

visas.summary: Andorra is not in the EU or Schengen, but you can only get there through Spain or France, so in practice you need to meet Schengen entry rules. To live there you apply for a residence authorization with the Immigration Service in Andorra. Some work-based permits are limited by quotas.

categories.name: Residence without lucrative activity (passive residence)
categories.forWho: People with enough wealth or income to live in Andorra without working there.
documents: Investment of at least EUR 600,000 in Andorran assets
Non-interest deposit of EUR 47,500 with the AFA (plus EUR 9,500 per dependent)

categories.name: Residence for professionals with international projection
categories.forWho: Professionals whose clients are mostly outside Andorra, who mainly work remotely from there.
documents: Non-interest deposit of EUR 47,500 with the AFA (plus EUR 9,500 per dependent)

categories.name: Residence and work authorization
categories.forWho: People hired by an Andorran employer. Some work permits are limited by quotas.
categories.processing: Varies. The employer usually starts the process.

categories.name: Self-employed residence and work
categories.forWho: People investing in their own Andorran company or working as a licensed liberal professional.
documents: Stake of more than 34% in an Andorran company, or authorization to practice your profession
Non-interest deposit of EUR 50,000 with the AFA (investment route)

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Many nationalities get a visa on arrival or visa-free entry, and others can get an e-visa in advance. Long stays need a residence visa and Emirates ID, usually sponsored by an employer or family member, or self-sponsored through the remote work, Green or Golden visas.

categories.name: Remote work (virtual work) residence visa
categories.forWho: People working remotely for an employer or their own company outside the UAE. Valid 1 year, self-sponsored.
categories.processing: Varies by emirate. Apply through ICP or GDRFA Dubai.
documents: Proof of remote employment or company ownership
Salary of at least USD 3,500 a month (or equivalent)

categories.name: Employment residence visa
categories.forWho: People hired by a UAE employer, who sponsors the visa.
categories.processing: Employer handles the work permit first. Varies.

categories.name: Green visa
categories.forWho: Skilled workers, freelancers and self-employed people, and investors or business partners. 5 years, no sponsor needed.

categories.name: Golden visa
categories.forWho: Investors, entrepreneurs, exceptional talent, outstanding students and some other groups. 5 or 10 years depending on category.

categories.name: Family residence visa
categories.forWho: Spouses, children and some relatives of UAE residents or citizens.

generalDocuments: Proof for your category (contract, salary, investment)
Medical fitness test (done in the UAE)

officialLinks.label: UAE government portal: visa and Emirates ID
Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

visas.summary: Afghanistan is run by the Taliban, and most governments, including the US and UK, advise against all travel. Visas are issued through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its missions abroad. Long-stay options are very limited and mostly tied to work for an organization or family ties.

categories.name: Work or business visa
categories.forWho: People sponsored by an organization or company operating in Afghanistan, such as aid groups.
categories.processing: Varies a lot by mission. Usually needs a sponsor letter.

categories.name: Family or residence visa
categories.forWho: Spouses and close family of Afghan citizens.

officialLinks.label: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: consular services
US State Department: Afghanistan travel advisory

visas.summary: Visitors from visa-exempt countries can usually stay up to 6 months, at the officer's discretion. Others apply for an e-visa in advance. Longer stays use the Nomad Digital Residence, a work permit, or residency through the Department of Immigration.

categories.name: Nomad Digital Residence (NDR)
categories.forWho: Remote workers employed outside Antigua and Barbuda earning at least US$50,000 a year. Valid up to 2 years.
categories.processing: Varies. Confirm with the Department of Immigration.
documents: Proof of employment outside the country

categories.name: Work permit
categories.forWho: People hired by a local employer or self-employed in Antigua and Barbuda.

categories.name: Permanent residence
categories.forWho: Long-term residents who have lived legally in the country for several years.

categories.name: Citizenship by Investment
categories.forWho: Investors making a qualifying contribution to the National Development Fund, real estate or a business.
categories.processing: Varies. Run by the Citizenship by Investment Unit.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Department of Immigration Antigua and Barbuda

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180. US citizens can currently stay up to 1 year visa-free. Longer stays use the Unique Permit, which combines residence and work.

categories.name: Unique Permit: Digital nomad
categories.forWho: Remote workers employed by or contracting for companies outside Albania.
categories.processing: Often several weeks. Confirm current times on e-Albania.
documents: Work contract or client agreements from abroad

categories.name: Unique Permit: Employment or self-employment
categories.forWho: People hired locally or running their own business in Albania.

categories.name: Residence: Pensioner
categories.forWho: Retirees with a pension from abroad.

categories.name: Residence: Property owner
categories.forWho: People who own real estate in Albania.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs: visa regime
US Embassy Albania: entering and residing

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free for up to 180 days a year, and many others can get an e-visa. For longer stays you apply for a temporary residence card (up to 1 year, renewable) with the Migration and Citizenship Service, which is moving applications fully online from 1 Nov 2026.

categories.name: Temporary residence: work
categories.forWho: People with a job in Armenia. Most need a work permit first.
categories.processing: Card issued within 30 days of applying, extendable by another 30.

categories.name: Temporary residence: business
categories.forWho: People running a business or self-employed in Armenia.

categories.name: Temporary residence: study or family
categories.forWho: Students, people of Armenian origin, and family of Armenian citizens or residents.

categories.name: Permanent residence
categories.forWho: Close family of Armenian citizens with 3+ years of legal residence, business owners, and people of Armenian origin. 5-year card.

generalDocuments: Valid passport and notarized Armenian translation
Documents supporting your grounds for residence

officialLinks.label: Migration and Citizenship Service: temporary residence
Ministry of Foreign Affairs: visa requirements

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free for tourism (up to 30 days per entry, 90 days a year), and tourist and business visas can be requested online. Living or working in Angola needs a work or residence visa through a consulate and the Migration and Foreigners Service (SME).

categories.name: Work visa
categories.forWho: People hired by an Angolan employer, who usually sponsors the application.
categories.processing: Varies by consulate. Often several weeks.

categories.name: Temporary stay or family visa
categories.forWho: Family of residents or citizens, and other approved long stays such as study.

categories.name: Residence permit
categories.forWho: People already in Angola on a qualifying visa who want to stay long term.
categories.processing: Varies. Handled by SME in Angola.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: SME (Migration and Foreigners Service): e-visa info

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free, usually up to 90 days. To live there you apply for temporary residence with the National Migration Office (DNM), mostly online through RaDEX, then go to an in-person appointment. After 3 years of temporary residence you can apply for permanent residence.

categories.name: Digital nomad (transitory residence)
categories.forWho: Remote workers for clients or employers abroad, from countries that do not need a tourist visa. Up to 180 days, extendable for the same period.
categories.processing: Varies. You apply in person while in Argentina.
documents: Proof of remote work (contract, company letter or invoices)

categories.name: Temporary residence: rentista or pensioner
categories.forWho: People living off a steady passive income or a pension from abroad.
documents: Proof of regular income or pension

categories.name: Temporary residence: worker
categories.forWho: People with a job offer from an Argentine employer.

categories.name: Temporary residence: student
categories.forWho: People enrolled at a recognized school or university in Argentina.

generalDocuments: Criminal record checks from home and from Argentina

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For long stays you usually apply for a residence permit at the Austrian consulate in your country, and pick it up in Austria.

categories.name: Red-White-Red Card
categories.forWho: Very highly qualified workers, skilled workers in shortage occupations, other key workers, graduates of Austrian universities, and start-up founders. Points based.
documents: Proof of qualifications for the points test

categories.name: EU Blue Card
categories.forWho: Graduates with a qualifying job offer above the salary threshold.

categories.name: Settlement permit, gainful employment excepted
categories.forWho: Retirees and financially independent people who will not work. Limited by a yearly quota.
documents: Regular monthly income of at least EUR 2,616.78 for a single person (2026)

categories.name: Student residence permit
categories.forWho: Students admitted to an Austrian university or college.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Settlement permit and other forms of settlement
Federal Ministry of the Interior: Red-White-Red Card

visas.summary: Every visitor except New Zealanders needs a visa or travel authority before flying, such as an ETA, eVisitor or Visitor visa (subclass 600), all applied for online. Living in Australia long term usually means an employer-sponsored or points-tested skilled visa, a working holiday visa, a student visa, or a partner visa.

categories.name: Skills in Demand visa (subclass 482)
categories.forWho: Skilled workers sponsored by an Australian employer.
categories.processing: Varies. Check the official processing times.

categories.name: Skilled Independent, Nominated or Regional (189, 190, 491)
categories.forWho: Skilled workers invited through SkillSelect based on points, occupation, and sometimes state nomination.
categories.processing: Invitation rounds plus processing. Can take many months.

categories.name: Working Holiday Maker (417 or 462)
categories.forWho: Young people from eligible countries, usually 18 to 30 (35 for some).

categories.name: Student visa (subclass 500)
categories.forWho: Students enrolled in a registered course in Australia.

categories.name: Partner visa
categories.forWho: Partners of Australian citizens, permanent residents or eligible New Zealanders.

officialLinks.label: Department of Home Affairs: visa listing

visas.summary: Aruba is part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands but has its own immigration rules and is not in Schengen. Visitors fill in an online ED card before travel, and some nationalities need a visa. Living or working there needs a residence permit from DIMAS, Aruba's immigration department. Dutch nationals follow a separate, simpler process.

categories.name: Work and residence permit
categories.forWho: People hired by an Aruban employer. Needs positive advice from the Labour Department (DPL) first.
categories.processing: Varies. Employer usually starts the process.

categories.name: Residence permit: business owner
categories.forWho: Owners or directors of an Aruban company.

categories.name: Residence permit: family
categories.forWho: Spouses, partners and children of Aruban residents or Dutch nationals living in Aruba.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Government of Aruba: work and residence permit

visas.summary: Many nationalities can get an e-visa online through the official portal, and some can visit visa-free. Visitors who stay beyond a short period must register their place of stay. Longer stays need a temporary residence permit from the State Migration Service, usually based on work, family, study, business or investment.

categories.name: Temporary residence: work permit
categories.forWho: People hired by an employer in Azerbaijan. The employer applies for the work permit.
categories.processing: Depends on the state fee paid. Usually up to 1 year at first, then renewable.

categories.name: Temporary residence: investment or property
categories.forWho: People who invest in Azerbaijan's economy, own real estate there, or hold a qualifying bank deposit or government securities.
categories.processing: Depends on the state fee paid.
documents: Proof of investment, property ownership or deposit (thresholds are set by the State Migration Service)

categories.name: Temporary residence: family or study
categories.forWho: Close relatives of Azerbaijani citizens or residents, and full-time students.
categories.processing: Depends on the state fee paid.

categories.name: Permanent residence
categories.forWho: People with at least 2 years of temporary residence on qualifying grounds. Usually needs a test on Azerbaijani law and language. 5-year permit, renewable.
categories.processing: Apply at least 3 months before your temporary permit expires.

generalDocuments: Passport valid 3+ months beyond the permit's expiry
Documents proving your grounds for residence

officialLinks.label: State Migration Service: temporary and permanent residence

visas.summary: Visitors from visa-exempt countries can stay up to 90 days within six months. For longer stays you apply for temporary residence, usually first at a Bosnia and Herzegovina embassy or consulate, then extend it locally with the Service for Foreigners' Affairs. Permits are issued for up to 1 year at a time.

categories.name: Temporary residence: work
categories.forWho: People with a work permit from a local employer, plus some exempt groups like university professors and volunteers.

categories.name: Temporary residence: family
categories.forWho: Spouses and partners of BiH citizens, and family reunification with residents.

categories.name: Temporary residence: property ownership
categories.forWho: People who own real estate in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

categories.name: Temporary residence: education
categories.forWho: Students enrolled at a school or university in BiH.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Service for Foreigners' Affairs: stay of foreigners
Service for Foreigners' Affairs: application documents

visas.summary: Most visitors do not need a visa for short stays, and the officer decides how long you get. Others apply online for an entry visa. Longer stays use the Welcome Stamp for remote workers, a work permit, or a special entry permit or residency through the Immigration Department.

categories.name: Barbados Welcome Stamp
categories.forWho: Remote workers earning at least US$50,000 a year from outside Barbados. Valid for 1 year, and you can reapply.
categories.processing: The program says applications are usually decided within about 7 business days.

categories.name: Work permit
categories.forWho: People hired by a Barbados employer, who applies for them. Short-term permits run up to 11 months, long-term up to 3 years.

categories.name: Special entry permit
categories.forWho: People who want to change the length or conditions of their stay in Barbados.

categories.name: Permanent residence or immigrant status
categories.forWho: Long-term residents and family of Barbadian citizens.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Most visitors need a visa from a Bangladesh mission, and some nationalities can get a visa on arrival. Applications start online through the Department of Immigration and Passports. Long stays are mainly employment or investor visas, which need a recommendation from BIDA or another approving authority, plus family and study visas.

categories.name: Employment (E) visa and work permit
categories.forWho: People hired by an organization in Bangladesh. You need an E-type visa to apply for the work permit, and BIDA or another approving authority issues the visa recommendation.

categories.name: Private investor (PI) visa
categories.forWho: Foreign investors putting money into a foreign-owned or joint venture business in Bangladesh.

categories.name: Family or study visa
categories.forWho: Spouses of Bangladeshi citizens, and students enrolled in Bangladesh.

officialLinks.label: Online visa application (Department of Immigration and Passports)
BIDA: visa types for foreigners working in Bangladesh

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For longer stays you apply for a long-stay (D) visa at the Belgian embassy or consulate for where you live, then register with your local commune in Belgium to get a residence card.

categories.name: Single permit (work and residence)
categories.forWho: People with a job offer from a Belgian employer. The employer applies to the regional authority.

categories.name: EU Blue Card
categories.forWho: Graduates with a qualifying job offer above the salary threshold.

categories.name: Professional card (self-employed)
categories.forWho: Freelancers and business owners who want to work self-employed in Belgium.

categories.name: Student visa
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a Belgian school or university.

categories.name: Family reunification
categories.forWho: Spouses, partners and children of people living in Belgium.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: FPS Foreign Affairs: visa for Belgium

visas.summary: Most governments, including the US and UK, advise against all or most travel to Burkina Faso because of armed conflict and terrorism, and entry rules can change at short notice. Short visits use an e-visa or a visa from an embassy. Long-stay options are limited and mostly tied to work for an organization or family, with a residence permit handled by the national police.

categories.name: Long-stay visa and residence permit: work
categories.forWho: People hired by an employer or organization in Burkina Faso, such as NGOs or mining companies.

categories.name: Long-stay visa and residence permit: family
categories.forWho: Spouses and close family of Burkinabe citizens or residents.

generalDocuments: Proof for your category (contract or family documents)

officialLinks.label: Burkina Faso e-visa (Ministry of Security, National Police)
US State Department: Burkina Faso travel information

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For long stays you apply for a type D visa at a Bulgarian embassy or consulate, with a mandatory interview, then get a residence permit from the Migration Directorate in Bulgaria.

categories.name: Work: single permit or EU Blue Card
categories.forWho: People with a job offer from a Bulgarian employer. Blue Card is for graduates above the salary threshold.
categories.processing: Varies. The employer usually starts the process in Bulgaria.

categories.name: Digital nomad residence
categories.forWho: Remote workers for employers or clients outside Bulgaria, added to the Foreigners Act in 2025. Income must be at least 50 times the Bulgarian minimum monthly wage per year. Granted for 1 year, extendable once.
categories.processing: Varies. New route, so check with the embassy first.
documents: Proof of remote work for a foreign employer or clients

categories.name: Long-stay residence: pensioner
categories.forWho: Retirees with a pension from abroad who want to live in Bulgaria.

categories.name: Family reunification
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of Bulgarian citizens or residents.

categories.name: Student visa
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a Bulgarian university.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: visa for Bulgaria

visas.summary: Many nationalities can get a visa on arrival or an e-visa for short stays. Living in Bahrain usually means a residence permit sponsored by an employer or family member. Self-sponsored options include Golden Residency for higher earners, property owners, retirees and talented individuals.

categories.name: Work residence permit
categories.forWho: People hired by a Bahraini employer, who sponsors the permit.

categories.name: Golden Residency
categories.forWho: Residents with higher salaries, property owners, retirees and talented individuals who meet the set criteria. Self-sponsored and renewable.
categories.processing: NPRA lists about 5 working days for the resident employee and retiree route.
documents: Salary certificate, pension or property documents, depending on the route

categories.name: Family residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of residents or Bahraini citizens.

generalDocuments: Proof for your category (contract, salary, property)

officialLinks.label: NPRA: Golden Residency for resident employees and retirees

visas.summary: Most visitors need a visa. Many get it on arrival after applying online in advance through the migration authority's website, and others apply at a Burundian embassy. The UK advises against all travel to some areas near the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Long-stay options are limited and mostly tied to work or family.

categories.name: Residence permit: work
categories.forWho: People hired by an employer or organization in Burundi.

categories.name: Residence permit: family
categories.forWho: Spouses and close family of Burundian citizens or residents.

visas.summary: Many nationalities can apply for an e-visa online before travel, and some are visa-exempt. Parts of northern Benin are under strong travel warnings. For long stays you get a residence card (carte de séjour) from the Directorate of Emigration and Immigration (DEI).

categories.name: Residence card: work
categories.forWho: People hired by an employer in Benin.

categories.name: Residence card: business
categories.forWho: People running their own business in Benin.

categories.name: Residence card: family or study
categories.forWho: Spouses and family of residents or citizens, and enrolled students.

visas.summary: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory with its own immigration rules, run by the Bermuda Department of Immigration (UK rules do not apply). Most visitors do not need a visa. Living there means a work permit through an employer or a permission to reside, and you cannot work without a permit.

categories.name: Work permit
categories.forWho: People hired by a Bermuda employer, who applies for the permit.

categories.name: Permission to reside on an annual basis
categories.forWho: Adults 18+ who will not work locally and can show adequate financial resources. Usually 1 year, renewable.

categories.name: Economic Investment Residential Certificate
categories.forWho: People who invest at least BD$2.5 million in Bermuda, such as real estate or a local business, and live there at least 90 days a year for 5 years.

categories.name: Permission to reside and attend college or school
categories.forWho: Full-time students accepted at a school or college in Bermuda.
categories.processing: Varies. Apply well before term starts.

categories.name: Spouse or partner of a Bermudian
categories.forWho: Spouses and partners of Bermudians or permanent resident certificate holders.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Government of Bermuda: residence permit application

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free for a short stay, and others need a visa from a Brunei mission. Longer stays are mostly through a work pass, a family pass, or a Long Term Pass, handled by the Immigration and National Registration Department.

categories.name: Work pass
categories.forWho: People hired by a Brunei employer, who starts the process.

categories.name: Family of foreign workers
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of work pass holders.

categories.name: Long Term Pass
categories.forWho: Family of Brunei citizens or permanent residents (social visit), company owners and investors (business visit), and needed experts (professional visit).

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free, usually up to 90 days a year, and others need a tourist visa from a consulate or on arrival. To live there you apply for temporary stay (permanencia temporal) of up to 3 years with the General Directorate of Migration, which can later lead to permanent stay.

categories.name: Temporary stay: work
categories.forWho: People with a job or contract in Bolivia.

categories.name: Temporary stay: family

visas.summary: Most governments, including the US and UK, advise against all travel to Belarus. visas.summary: The US and many other governments advise against all travel to the Central African Republic. Entry and stay are handled by the Public Security Police Force, and working needs a non-resident worker permit sponsored by an employer.

categories.name: Non-resident worker (employer sponsored)

categories.name: Talent programs

visas.summary: Most visitors need a visa. Since January 2025 it's an e-visa: fill in the online form through ANRPTS before you board, and you may pay on arrival. Visas are also issued at Mauritanian embassies. The US says reconsider travel, and do not travel to the far north or within 60 miles of the Mali and Algeria borders. Long stays are mostly tied to work or family.

categories.name: Work and residence

categories.name: Family residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of citizens or residents.

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For longer stays non-EU nationals get a residence permit through Identita (for work, study and family) or through Residency Malta Agency (for the nomad permit and investor residence).

categories.forWho: Remote workers employed by or freelancing for clients outside Malta.
categories.processing: Varies. Run by Residency Malta Agency, permits are valid for 1 year and can be renewed.
documents: Proof of remote work for a foreign employer or clients
Proof of income above the program threshold

categories.name: Single permit (employment)

categories.processing: Often several weeks. The employer usually applies through Identita.

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit without arranging a visa first, and some must get one before travel. For long stays, the free Premium Visa lets you live there for up to 1 year (renewable) while earning from abroad. Working locally needs an Occupation Permit through the Economic Development Board.

categories.name: Premium Visa
categories.forWho: Remote workers, retirees and long-stay visitors whose income comes from outside Mauritius. Up to 1 year, renewable. No local work.
categories.processing: Applied for online and sent by email. No fee.
documents: Proof your income and business are outside Mauritius

categories.name: Occupation Permit
categories.forWho: Professionals hired by a company in Mauritius. Includes a Young Professional route for eligible graduates.
categories.processing: Varies. Applications go through the EDB.

categories.name: Residence permit: retired non-citizen
categories.forWho: Retirees aged 50+ who transfer a set minimum income to Mauritius. Valid 10 years and renewable.
documents: Proof of pension or income transferred to Mauritius (at least USD 24,000 a year or USD 2,000 a month)

categories.name: Residence through property
categories.forWho: People buying property under EDB-approved schemes like IRS, RES, PDS, Smart City or Ground+2 apartments.
documents: Property purchase under an approved scheme

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Most nationalities get a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival, as long as they have a return ticket, a confirmed booking and enough funds (Israeli passports are not admitted). categories.name: Dependent visa

categories.name: Corporate Resident Visa
categories.forWho: Foreign investors who invest at least USD 1 million in the Maldives, keep a USD 250,000 fixed deposit for 5 years, or invest USD 250,000 in a government-approved project.
categories.processing: Varies. Apply through the ONEGov Portal.

generalDocuments: Proof for your category (job offer, sponsor letter, etc.)

visas.summary: Many visitors need a visa, which you can apply for online through the official e-visa portal, and some can also get one on arrival. Long stays need a permit from the Department of Immigration, such as a work or residence permit.

categories.name: Temporary Employee Permit (TEP)

categories.name: Business Residence Permit
categories.forWho: Investors and people running a business in Malawi.

categories.name: Student permit
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a school or university in Malawi.

generalDocuments: Proof for your category (job offer, sponsor letter, etc.)

categories.forWho: Retirees with higher pension income, or people with close family ties.

categories.name: Family reunification

visas.summary: Puerto Rico is a US territory and follows US immigration law. US citizens can move there freely with no visa. Everyone else needs the same visa, ESTA or green card they would need for the mainland US. Puerto Rico's tax incentives (Act 60) do not give any immigration status.

categories.name: US citizens
categories.forWho: US citizens, who can live and work in Puerto Rico with no visa or passport needed.

categories.name: US work visa
categories.forWho: Non-US citizens with a job offer from a US or Puerto Rico employer (for example H-1B or L-1).
categories.processing: Varies. Check USCIS and the State Department for current times.

categories.name: Green card (permanent residence)
categories.forWho: Family of US citizens or permanent residents, sponsored workers, or investors under the EB-5 program.
categories.processing: Often months to years, depending on category and country.

categories.name: Student visa (F-1)
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a certified school or university in Puerto Rico.

generalDocuments: Completed DS-160 or other US application form
Proof of the reason for your stay (job offer, school admission, family tie)

visas.summary: Israel controls all entry to the West Bank and Gaza, so foreigners follow Israeli entry rules, including the ETA-IL for visa-exempt travelers, and usually enter through Israel or from Jordan via the Allenby crossing when it is open. Gaza is effectively closed to most foreigners, and many governments advise against travel there and urge caution in the West Bank. Long-stay options are very limited and mostly tied to family or NGO and organizational work.

categories.name: NGO or organizational work permit
categories.forWho: Staff of international organizations, NGOs and institutions working in the West Bank, with permits coordinated through Israeli authorities.
categories.processing: Varies and can be slow or uncertain.

categories.name: Family residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and family of Palestinian ID holders. Approval depends on Israeli-controlled population registry procedures.
categories.processing: Often very slow, can take years.

generalDocuments: Letter from your employer or organization
Proof of family relationship (for family cases)

officialLinks.label: Israel Population and Immigration Authority: ETA-IL
US State Department: Israel, West Bank and Gaza advisory
UK government: Palestinian Territories entry requirements

visas.summary: Schengen country. For long stays you get a national (D) visa at a consulate, then finish your residence permit with AIMA in Portugal.

categories.name: D7: Passive income visa
categories.forWho: Retirees and people with steady passive income.
categories.processing: Legal decision target is about 60 days from a complete application. Real timelines often run longer.

categories.name: D8: Digital nomad visa
categories.forWho: Remote workers earning from outside Portugal.
categories.processing: About 60 days legal target, often longer in practice.
documents: Proof of income for the last months

categories.name: D1: Work visa
categories.forWho: People with a job contract in Portugal.

categories.name: D4: Study visa
categories.forWho: Students accepted by a Portuguese institution.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Many visitors can enter visa-free or get a visa on arrival for a short stay, and passengers must submit the Palau Entry Form before arrival. US citizens can live and work in Palau under the Compact of Free Association. Other foreigners staying long term usually need an employer-sponsored work permit.

categories.name: US citizens (Compact of Free Association)
categories.forWho: US citizens, who can live and work in Palau without a visa.
categories.processing: No visa needed. A valid passport is required.

categories.name: Work permit
categories.forWho: Foreign workers hired by a Palau employer, who sponsors the permit.
categories.processing: Varies. The employer usually starts the process.

categories.name: Spouse or dependent permit
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of Palauan citizens or of sponsored workers.

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free, and others need a visa from a Paraguayan consulate. Paraguay is known for a fairly simple residency process: most people start with temporary residence through the National Migration Directorate in Asuncion, then apply for permanent residence later.

categories.name: Temporary residence
categories.forWho: Most foreigners moving to Paraguay for work, study, family or to live on their own funds.

categories.name: MERCOSUR temporary residence
categories.forWho: Citizens of MERCOSUR and associated countries, who get a simpler route.

categories.name: Permanent residence
categories.forWho: Temporary residents who have held their status long enough and want to stay for good.

categories.name: Permanent residence: investor (SUACE)
categories.forWho: People with an investment project recognized by the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, which lets you apply straight for permanent residence.
documents: Investor certificate (Constancia de Inversionista) from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce
Plan to invest at least USD 70,000 within 2 years and create local jobs

generalDocuments: Local police record and address in Paraguay

officialLinks.label: Ministry of Industry and Commerce: guide for foreign investors (PDF, Spanish)

visas.summary: Citizens of many countries can enter visa-free, and others apply for an e-visa on the Hayya platform. Living in Qatar almost always means a residence permit (QID) sponsored by an employer or family member, issued by the Ministry of Interior. Property purchase above set amounts can also lead to residence.

categories.name: Work residence permit
categories.forWho: People hired by a Qatari employer, who sponsors the visa and residence permit.
categories.processing: Varies. The employer handles most steps.
documents: Medical exam and fingerprinting in Qatar

categories.name: Family residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of residents who meet the sponsor salary and housing rules.

categories.name: Property-linked residence
categories.forWho: Foreigners buying qualifying real estate in designated areas above the required value.

categories.name: Permanent residence card
categories.forWho: A small group of long-term residents and certain family members who meet strict conditions.

visas.summary: Schengen country since 2025. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For longer stays you apply for a long-stay (D) visa through the e-Visa portal and a Romanian consulate, then get a residence permit from the General Inspectorate for Immigration (IGI) in Romania.

categories.name: Digital nomad visa
categories.forWho: Remote workers employed by, or running, companies registered outside Romania, earning at least 3 times the Romanian average gross monthly salary.
documents: Proof of remote employment or business ownership abroad
Proof of income for the last 6 months

categories.name: Employment visa
categories.forWho: People hired by a Romanian employer, who gets a work permit for you first.
categories.processing: Varies. The work permit comes first, then the visa.

categories.name: Business or self-employment visa
categories.forWho: People investing in or running a business in Romania.

categories.name: Family reunification
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of foreigners living legally in Romania.

categories.name: Study visa
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a Romanian university.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: e-Visa portal

visas.summary: Serbia is not in the EU or Schengen. Many nationalities can visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180, while others need a visa. For longer stays you apply for temporary residence (often the single permit for residence and work), and many applications can now be filed online through the government's portal for foreigners.

categories.name: Single permit (temporary residence and work)
categories.forWho: People hired by a Serbian employer. Covers residence and work in one application.

categories.name: Temporary residence: business or self-employment
categories.forWho: Founders and owners of a registered company or sole proprietorship in Serbia.

categories.name: Temporary residence: property ownership
categories.forWho: Foreigners who own real estate in Serbia. There is also a D visa for this purpose.

categories.name: Temporary residence: family or study
categories.forWho: Spouses and family of Serbian citizens or residents, and students enrolled in Serbia.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Welcome to Serbia (official portal for foreigners)
Ministry of Foreign Affairs: visa regime
Welcome to Serbia: D visa for real estate owners

visas.summary: Most Western governments advise against travel to Russia. Many nationalities can get a single-entry unified e-visa for stays up to 30 days. Long stays are limited and mostly go through employer-sponsored work visas, study, family ties, or a temporary residence permit.

categories.name: Work visa (employer invitation)
categories.forWho: People hired by a Russian employer that gets a work permit and invitation for them.
categories.processing: Varies. The employer's paperwork usually takes the longest.

categories.name: Temporary residence permit (RVP)
categories.forWho: People with family ties, Russian heritage, or other grounds set by law. Many applicants fall under a yearly quota.

categories.name: Shared values visa
categories.forWho: Nationals of countries on a Russian government list who say they do not support their own country's policies and share Russia's "traditional values". It leads to a temporary residence permit under simplified rules.

categories.name: Student visa
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a Russian university.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Invitation or sponsor letter (for most long-stay visas)
Medical certificate including HIV test (for long stays)

visas.summary: Rwanda gives visas on arrival to visitors of all nationalities, and some get visa waivers. To live there, you usually enter on a visa, then apply for a permit online through IremboGov with the Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration.

categories.name: Work permit (Class H)
categories.forWho: Skilled workers hired by a Rwandan employer or in a job on the Occupations in Demand list.
categories.processing: Official guidance says about 7 days for a complete application.

categories.name: Investor or entrepreneur permit
categories.forWho: People investing in or running a business in Rwanda.

categories.name: Assured income permit (Class K)
categories.forWho: Retirees and people with income from abroad who won't work in Rwanda.

categories.name: Dependent permit (Class M)
categories.forWho: Family of Rwandan citizens or of foreign residents.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration

visas.summary: Many nationalities can get a tourist e-visa online, valid for a year with stays of up to 90 days. Living in Saudi Arabia usually means an employer-sponsored work visa and residence card (iqama), or Premium Residency, which doesn't need a sponsor.

categories.name: Employment visa (iqama)
categories.forWho: People hired by a Saudi employer. The employer gets the visa authorization first.
categories.processing: Varies. Once issued, the visa is valid for 3 months from the issue date.

categories.name: Premium Residency
categories.forWho: Investors, entrepreneurs, real estate owners, special talent and gifted people, or anyone choosing the limited or unlimited duration option, who want residence without a sponsor.
categories.processing: The official government service page lists 90 working days. Apply on the Premium Residency platform.

categories.name: Family visit or dependent residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of people living and working in Saudi Arabia.

officialLinks.label: Example: Saudi embassy in Canada, employment visa

visas.summary: Many visitors get a visitor permit on arrival. For long stays you need approval from the Director of Immigration before you come, and long-term visas are usually issued for up to 2 years.

categories.name: Long-term employment visa
categories.forWho: People with a job offer from a Solomon Islands employer. Work permits are handled by the Labor Division.
categories.processing: Varies. Approval is needed before you travel.

categories.name: Long-term special purpose visa
categories.forWho: Volunteers, researchers, religious workers and other special purposes.

categories.name: Long-term student visa
categories.forWho: Students enrolled in a course in Solomon Islands.

categories.name: Family or dependent visa
categories.forWho: Spouses and children of long-term visa holders, and people with family ties.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Seychelles is visa-free for all nationalities: you get a visitor permit on arrival and must complete the electronic border form before traveling. To live or work there you need a permit from Immigration and Civil Status.

categories.name: Gainful Occupation Permit (GOP)
categories.forWho: Employees and self-employed people working in Seychelles. The employer applies for staff.
categories.processing: Official site says GOPs can be collected 1 to 5 days after applying, once the employment ministry approves.
documents: Employer application and approval from the employment ministry
Project memorandum to the Seychelles Investment Board (for new businesses)

categories.name: Residence permit
categories.forWho: People with family ties to Seychelles or who will make a special economic, social or cultural contribution. You can't work on it.
documents: Bank guarantee of at least SCR 20,000

categories.name: Permanent residence
categories.forWho: Long-term residents approved by the Minister. Holders can live and work without a separate permit.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Sudan is in an active armed conflict. The US advises against all travel, and the UK advises against all travel to parts of the country. Everyone needs a visa from a Sudanese embassy, and long-stay options are basically limited to employer or family sponsorship.

categories.name: Work or business visa (sponsored)
categories.forWho: People sponsored by an employer or organization operating in Sudan, such as aid groups.
categories.processing: Varies a lot. Embassy services can be slow or disrupted.

categories.name: Family visit or residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and close family of Sudanese citizens or residents.

generalDocuments: Passport valid 6+ months, with no Israeli stamps or visas
Registration with the Aliens Department within 3 days of arrival

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For longer stays you apply for a residence permit with the Swedish Migration Agency, usually online, and most people need it approved before moving.

categories.name: Work permit
categories.forWho: People with a job offer from a Swedish employer.
categories.processing: Varies. Check the Migration Agency's processing time tool.
documents: Job offer meeting Swedish pay and insurance terms
Salary of at least 90% of the Swedish median wage (SEK 34,470 a month as of June 2026)

categories.name: EU Blue Card
categories.forWho: Highly qualified workers with a job of at least 6 months paying 1.25 times the average gross salary.

categories.name: Residence permit for self-employment
categories.forWho: People starting or buying a business in Sweden.
documents: Business plan and experience in the field
Proof of funds to support yourself

categories.name: Residence permit for studies

categories.processing: Varies. Apply early before the semester.

Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit Singapore without a visa, but everyone must submit the free SG Arrival Card within 3 days before arriving. Living there means getting a pass: work passes come from the Ministry of Manpower, and student and residence passes from ICA.

categories.name: Employment Pass (EP)
categories.forWho: Professionals, managers and executives earning at least SGD 5,600 a month who pass the COMPASS points test. Your employer applies.
categories.processing: Varies. Check MOM for current times.

categories.name: S Pass
categories.forWho: Mid-level skilled workers earning at least SGD 3,300 a month.

categories.name: ONE Pass (Overseas Networks and Expertise Pass)
categories.forWho: Top talent in business, arts, sports, science or research. Lets you work for multiple companies.

categories.name: EntrePass
categories.forWho: Founders starting a venture-backed or innovative business in Singapore.

categories.name: Dependent's Pass or Long-Term Visit Pass
categories.forWho: Spouses, children and some other family of EP or S Pass holders.

generalDocuments: Completed application (usually filed by your employer)
Marriage or birth certificates (for family passes)

officialLinks.label: Ministry of Manpower: passes and permits

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For longer stays you apply for a temporary residence permit at a Slovenian embassy or consulate, or at a local administrative unit if you're already legally in Slovenia.

categories.name: Temporary residence permit: digital nomad
categories.forWho: Non-EU remote workers employed by or freelancing for businesses outside Slovenia. Launched Nov 2025, valid up to 1 year and not renewable.

Monthly income of at least 2 times Slovenia's average net salary

categories.processing: Varies. Often several weeks to a few months.

categories.name: Temporary residence: self-employment or business
categories.forWho: People running their own business or working as self-employed in Slovenia.

categories.name: Temporary residence: study or family reunification
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a Slovenian school, and family of residents.

Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For longer stays you apply for temporary residence for one specific purpose, at a Slovak embassy or at the Foreign Police in Slovakia if you're already there legally.

categories.name: Temporary residence: employment
categories.forWho: People with a job offer from a Slovak employer.
categories.processing: Legal deadline is usually 90 days, extendable by 30 in complicated cases.

categories.name: EU Blue Card
categories.forWho: Highly qualified workers with a job offer meeting the salary threshold.

categories.name: Temporary residence: business
categories.forWho: Self-employed people and company founders. Since July 2025 you must apply at an embassy abroad, and there's a yearly cap.

categories.name: Temporary residence: study
categories.forWho: Students accepted at a Slovak school.

visas.summary: Many nationalities need a visa, and the Immigration Department runs an official eVisa portal. To live or work there, you apply for residence and work permits through the Unified Permit portal after arriving.

categories.name: Work permit

categories.name: Residence permit
categories.forWho: Foreigners living in Sierra Leone long term, including investors, retirees and family of residents.

categories.name: Student residence permit

visas.summary: San Marino isn't in Schengen, but you can only get there through Italy, so Schengen rules apply in practice. Stays over 3 months need a stay permit (up to 1 year, renewable) or a residence permit from the San Marino authorities.

categories.name: Stay permit (permesso di soggiorno)
categories.forWho: People staying 3 months to 1 year for work, family, study, tourism and other set purposes.

categories.name: Elective residence
categories.forWho: People who make and keep a property or financial investment in San Marino. You can't work in the public sector.

categories.name: Atypical residence (facilitated tax regime)
categories.forWho: People earning income from abroad who haven't been tax resident in San Marino before.

categories.name: Registered residence
categories.forWho: Family of San Marino citizens, people starting a business there, or managers of San Marino companies.

visas.summary: Many nationalities, including ECOWAS citizens, can visit Senegal without a visa, but rules change, so check with a Senegalese embassy before you go. If you settle there for more than 3 months, you apply for a foreigner's residence card with the foreigners police in Dakar (or the local police elsewhere).

categories.name: Residence card: employment
categories.forWho: People working for an employer in Senegal.
categories.processing: Varies. You get a receipt to use while the card is processed.

Refundable deposit at the Caisse de Dépôts et Consignations

categories.name: Residence card: family or sponsored
categories.forWho: Spouses and family of residents, or people supported by a sponsor in Senegal.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Handwritten application letter to the Minister of the Interior

visas.summary: Most governments advise against all travel to Somalia because of terrorism, kidnapping and armed conflict. Since 1 Sep 2025 visitors must get an electronic travel authorization (eTAS) online before departure. Long-stay options are limited, mostly work for an organization or family sponsorship.

categories.name: Work or business visa (sponsored)
categories.forWho: People working for a company, NGO or international organization in Somalia.
categories.processing: Varies. Your sponsor usually starts the process.

categories.name: Family residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and close family of Somali citizens or residents.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)

visas.summary: South Sudan has ongoing armed conflict and high crime, and the US and UK advise against all travel. Everyone needs a visa, usually through the official e-visa portal. Long stays are mostly for aid, NGO or company work, and you need a work permit from the Ministry of Labor too.

categories.name: Work visa and work permit
categories.forWho: People employed by an NGO, UN agency or company operating in South Sudan.

categories.name: Family or dependent residence

visas.summary: Some nationalities can visit visa-free for short stays, and others apply online through the Migration and Borders Service (SMF) e-visa portal. Longer stays for work, study or business need the right visa and then residence from the SMF.

categories.name: Work visa and residence
categories.forWho: People hired by an employer in São Tomé and Príncipe.

categories.name: Family residence

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit El Salvador without a visa, and it's part of the CA-4 area with Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, where a 90-day limit can apply across all four. categories.name: Permanent residence (residencia definitiva)

visas.summary: Most governments, including the UK and US, advise against all travel to Syria. Visitors need a visa, which can be applied for through the official Syrian e-visa site. Long-stay options are very limited and mostly come down to work for an organization or family ties.

categories.name: Work or business visa (sponsored)
categories.forWho: People working for an organization or company in Syria that sponsors them.

categories.name: Family residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and close family of Syrian citizens.

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit Eswatini visa-free for up to 30 days, and you can apply for a 30-day extension with the Ministry of Home Affairs. Stays beyond 60 days, or any work or study, need a temporary residence permit.

categories.name: Student pass
categories.forWho: Students enrolled at a school or university in Eswatini.

categories.name: Dependent pass

visas.summary: The UK advises against all travel to parts of Chad, including the north, the Lake Chad region and areas near the borders, and against all but essential travel to the rest, including N'Djamena. categories.name: Work or business visa (sponsored)
categories.forWho: People employed by a company, NGO or organization in Chad.

categories.name: Family residence
categories.forWho: Spouses and close family of Chadian citizens or residents.
